evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=52.0h = 11.71 mg/L (simulated_online_sensor), well above 2.0 mg/L minimum; P assay (t=48h, available 52h) = 3.16 g/L
Source controls at 48h: P = 3.06, 3.02, 2.98 g/L; source DO2 troughs ~7.4-8.2 mg/L around 72h then recovers - no oxygen-constraint history
physical_forward_model strong_feed_reduction: 621.5 kg, min DO 10.85 mg/L, feasible; sensitivity range 616.3-627.3 kg, min DO 9.90-11.60
physical_forward_model reduce_feed: 595.5 kg (range 590.1-602.0), min DO 9.95; combined: 595.5 kg, min DO 10.29
physical_forward_model keep: 576.3 kg (range 576.3-582.8), min DO 9.07 post-decision; increase_air: 576.3 kg, no mass gain
submission.rationale: At the decision time (t=52h), the receiving fermentation shows no oxygen stress (DO2 11.7 mg/L, floor is 2.0) and productivity tracking the source batches (P=3.16 g/L vs 2.98-3.06 g/L at 48h). The nominal source-calibrated forward model indicates all feed-reduction actions are oxygen-feasible with improved terminal product mass because reduced feed lowers dilution and slightly improves DO margin: keep 576.3 kg, reduce_feed 595.5 kg, combined 595.5 kg, strong_feed_reduction 621.5 kg, all with zero below-limit hours and min DO far above 2.0. Strong feed reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) gives the highest mass; its 5-member sensitivity range (616.3-627.3 kg, min DO 9.9-11.6) does not overlap even the best of KEEP (576.3-582.8 kg), so the advantage is robust to the assumed parameter spread while retaining large oxygen margin. I therefore recommend strong_feed_reduction.
submission.uncertainty: The physics model is a source-calibrated nominal prediction, not the hidden receiving realization; source and receiving kinetics differ, and the product-mass gain from feed reduction depends on model structure not directly verified by observations. Late strong feed cuts could in reality slow production more than the model suggests, though the sensitivity members vary kinetics and still show a clear advantage. Oxygen-constraint risk is very low (min DO stays above ~9.9 mg/L in all sensitivity members), so the main uncertainty is magnitude of product-mass benefit, not feasibility.
